title: Microsoft Cancels Claude Code Licenses, Shifting to GitHub Copilot CLI
description: Microsoft began canceling Claude Code licenses for thousands of developers across Windows, Microsoft 365, Outlook, and other teams. The cancellation deadline is June 30, 2026, aligning with end of fiscal year. Decision driven by financial motives and AI tool costs spiraling beyond budget despite falling token prices. Microsoft is shifting developers to GitHub Copilot CLI.
author: Windows Central / Hacker News

title: Kanbots: Open Source Kanban Running Parallel AI Agents on Every Card
description: Kanbots v1.0 launched as an open source (MIT licensed) kanban board that runs parallel Claude Code or Codex agents on every card, each in its own git worktree. Features include autopilot mode with personas splitting work, decision prompts, local-first with zero servers, cost analytics, and GitHub integration with draft PRs. Includes MCP server for integration with Cursor and Claude Desktop.
author: leodavinci1

title: Deno 2.8 Released
description: Deno 2.8 released with updates to the JavaScript/TypeScript runtime.
author: Deno team

title: Bun Support Now Limited and Deprecated in yt-dlp
description: The yt-dlp project announced that Bun support is now limited and deprecated, reflecting ongoing challenges in JavaScript runtime ecosystem compatibility.
author: yt-dlp team

title: Superset: IDE for the Agents Era (YC P26)
description: Superset launched as an 'IDE for the agents era' from Y Combinator P26 batch, positioning itself as a development environment designed for AI agent workflows.
author: Superset team / YC

title: Project Glasswing: An Initial Update from Anthropic
description: Anthropic published an initial update on Project Glasswing, though the specific page was not accessible. The project was trending on Hacker News with significant community interest.
author: Anthropic

title: The Memory Shortage and AI: HBM Impact on Consumer Electronics
description: Simon highlighted David Oks' explanation of how AI data centers are causing memory shortages. With only three major memory manufacturers and fixed wafer capacity, HBM (high-bandwidth memory for GPUs) allocation is increasing from 2% to 20% by end of 2026. Since HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity per GB than DDR/LPDDR, this is causing consumer electronics to become more expensive.
author: Simon Willison

title: FTC Settlement on 'Active Listening' AI Marketing Fraud
description: FTC announced Cox Media Group and two other firms will pay nearly $1 million to settle charges about deceiving customers regarding 'Active Listening' AI-powered marketing. The service claimed to listen to conversations through smart devices but actually just resold email lists from data brokers at markup. Simon noted this confirms his theory that 'active listening' was just marketing-speak for existing ad targeting.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette Agent: First Release of Extensible AI Assistant for Datasette
description: Simon Willison announced Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant that integrates LLM capabilities with Datasette. This represents the culmination of three years of work on his LLM Python library. Features include running commands in Fly Sprites sandbox, 'View SQL query' buttons for charts, improved handling of truncated responses, and permission-based tool availability.
author: Simon Willison

title: SpaceX-Anthropic Deal: $1.25 Billion/Month for Compute Capacity
description: SpaceX entered into Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to compute capacity across COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May and June 2026 at reduced fees. Agreements terminable upon 90 days notice.
author: Simon Willison (citing SpaceX S-1)

title: How Fast is 10 Tokens Per Second Really?
description: Simon highlighted an interactive HTML app by Mike Veerman that simulates LLM token output speeds from 5/second to 800/second, helping users understand what different token speeds actually feel like in practice.
author: Simon Willison

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash and Google I/O 2026: Prompt Injection Concerns
description: Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash and announced Gemini Spark, a personal AI agent that connects natively with Google apps. Simon expressed concerns about prompt injection risks, noting that Gemini Spark will route traffic through an Agent Gateway enforcing DLP policies in isolated VMs. Also noted Google is retiring the open source Gemini CLI for the closed-source Antigravity CLI.
author: Simon Willison

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: More Expensive, But Google Plan to Use It for Everything
description: Simon analyzed Google's release of Gemini 3.5 Flash at Google I/O 2026, noting it went straight to general availability without preview designation and Google is using it across many key products. The piece discusses pricing implications and Google's strategy.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Last Six Months in LLMs in Five Minutes - PyCon US 2026 Lightning Talk
description: Simon presented a lightning talk at PyCon US 2026 with annotated slides covering the last six months of developments in the LLM space, providing a rapid-fire overview of key trends and advances.
author: Simon Willison

title: Government Digital Service on AI, Open Code and Vulnerability Risk
description: The UK Government Digital Service published guidance stating 'Keep open by default' in response to NHS's decision to close open source repositories after vulnerability reports. GDS noted that making everything private adds delivery/policy costs and reduces reuse/scrutiny. Terence Eden interpreted this as a major escalation in civil service disagreement.
author: Simon Willison (citing Terence Eden and UK GDS)
